status: About 55 arms scored at 16k (one seed, eval_size 184). Best so far: the recipe trained on a pool that mixes 1k-2k-token rows with the 4k-16k rows, 2.35x fewer FLOPs than dense LoRA at matched loss and 1.25x the plain recipe; a gold-aware keep arm is 1.26x the recipe; rows <= 5k 1.35x at a shallow level. Deeper two-seed confirmations are running. The reference is now the cheaper of dense LoRA at LR 1e-5 and 2e-5, which lowers the recipe to 1.7x at the 100-step level (1.4x on the worst task). Closed as negative: frozen no-grad prefix, earlier cuts, FFN skip, early-exit-loss selection, detached context, input-level token exit (with or without the drop-CPT base), higher LR, 8 rows/step, keep below 20%/7%, random keep. Nothing is near 10x: every idea that touches blocks 0-6 or the context's gradient loses more per step than it saves.
setup: Each method trains with its own forward, optimiser and real LR schedule on the same first batches of the pool (16 rows/step, 2 GPUs).

At fixed steps the dense forward (full context, no dropping, adapters on) is scored on held-out rows from the CTC-suite eval files: teacher-forced answer CE, 16 rows per task and length (4k, 8k, 16k) except reorder at 16k, where only 8 eval rows fit in 16,384 tokens; eval_size 184.

Score = training FLOPs the dense reference needs to reach a loss level divided by the FLOPs the method needs to reach the same level, on the mean loss and on the worst task. Peak GPU memory is logged per step.
One iteration is under 15 minutes. Every 2-3 hours the most promising methods get a larger FLOP-matched training run with generation-graded evals.

Data caveats: the 16k training cells use fewer documents per row than the eval (contradiction 324 vs 379, outlier 96 vs 111, reorder 90 vs 116) so rows fit in 16,384 tokens; the 16k held-out rows are the short tail of the eval rung (70, 303, 8 and 497 of 500 rows fit for contradiction, outlier, reorder, qdmatch_nq). About 46% of the documents in a qdmatch_nq held-out row also occur in training rows (no gold overlap, no prompt overlap).
Memory is reported as the step's transient (peak minus the weights and optimizer state held before the step), since under activation checkpointing the absolute peak is dominated by the fixed part.

For runs that stop before reaching a reference level, the table also gives iso-loss ratios at the run's own final loss: FLOPs the dense-LoRA reference (and the recipe) need to reach that loss divided by the run's FLOPs. These are generous to a run whose final loss is shallow, because the reference curves are only probed every 10-25 steps.

log.text: First larger validation started: full-epoch dense LoRA (three FLOP budgets), recipe (two seeds) and dense full FT on mtb16k with generation-graded evals at 4k / 8k / 16k; plus full-epoch dense-loss curves for dense LoRA and the recipe.

Short-row pools: recipe on the 50/50 and 80/20 mixes is 1.25x the recipe at matched loss; short rows alone 0.74x; dense LoRA on any of them is behind the recipe. Detached context: negative (context forward-only without drops 0.15x of the recipe's efficiency; every 4th step dense 0.44x). Early-exit-loss selection: negative (ridge router is better at equal keep). Input-level token exit at ratio 0.05-0.10 does not train from the standard or the drop-CPT base. Dense LoRA at LR 2e-5 is a slightly better reference (0.126 vs 0.131 at step 100); LR 4e-5 is worse.
Two ideas closed as negative: frozen no-grad prefix with earlier cuts, and FFN skip for context tokens. Both show that blocks 0-6 need every token, every FFN and their own gradient.

Short-row pools built (mean row 1.6k / 3.1k / 5.4k tokens vs 9.1k) and running on Beaker with dense LoRA and the recipe. Detached-context screen moved to Beaker. Reorder is the task every cheap arm loses on (0.45-0.60 vs 0.33).

Lambda (2 x A100 per run) and Beaker (2 x H100 per run) staged and verified: step-0 loss matches Berkeley. Six Beaker jobs launched (LR and rows-per-step sweeps, dense-LoRA reference LR check, keep ladder down to 2% / 1%).

References done: dense full FT 0.135 and dense LoRA 0.131 held-out CE at step 100; recipe 0.125 at step 200 for 0.22x dense per step. Reorder dominates the mean loss (about 0.33 for all three; the other tasks 0.04-0.11).
CPT search: a usable token-exit CPT base (dropstruct, tokens leave from block 8, 64M CPT tokens) and its dense-CPT control exist and are staged; the 1B-token FFN-drop CPT base was deleted on 10-30.

Pool mtb16k and held-out v2 final after one rebuild (16k cells regenerated with fewer documents so rows fit in 16,384 tokens). References and baselines launched on 6 GPUs; all 8 preemptive_high GPUs in use.

Seven idea agents started (no-grad prefix + early cuts, gold-aware stochastic keep, early-layer loss selection, detached context, FLOP-aware row sampling, FFN skip for context tokens, token-drop CPT base search). Staging agents started for Lambda and Beaker.
Loop requested: tasks switched to contradiction, outlier, reorder, qdmatch_nq at 4k-16k; target 10-20x FLOPs and 5-10x less peak memory.

ideas.title: Dense full fine-tune and dense LoRA at 4k-16k
ideas.what: Reference loss-vs-FLOPs curves (probes every 10 steps to step 100). Every speedup on this page is read against these.
ideas.result: Held-out CE at step 50 / 100: dense full FT 0.176 / 0.135, dense LoRA LR 1e-5 0.170 / 0.131, dense LoRA LR 2e-5 0.126 at step 100 (dense LoRA costs 0.74x dense per step). The reference is the cheaper of the three at each loss level.

ideas.title: Current recipe (router, keep 20% after block 7, 7% after block 16)
ideas.what: The 8k recipe unchanged at 4k-16k on the new tasks, plus random keep at the same budget.
ideas.result: Recipe: 0.22x dense per step, 1.7x fewer FLOPs than the tuned dense-LoRA reference to the 100-step level, 1.4x on the worst task. Random keep at the same budget: 0.54x of the recipe's efficiency; random keep 9%: 0.42x; keep 10%/3.5%: 0.71x; 5%/2%: 0.55x; 2%/1%: 0.27x.

ideas.title: Frozen no-grad prefix + earlier cuts
ideas.what: Blocks 0-k run forward-only (no backward, no stored activations), tokens dropped from block 2-4 onward in more stages. Attacks the 0.2x/step floor of blocks 0-6 and the memory peak.
ideas.result: Negative. Freezing blocks 0-6 (forward-only) with the recipe's cuts: 0.149x dense per step, 0.282 held-out CE at step 60 vs about 0.19 for the recipe; deeper freezing is worse (0.399 / 0.491 / 0.647 with the boundary at block 7 / 16 / 20 plus earlier cuts). Earlier cuts alone (first cut at block 2) also trail the recipe per FLOP. Transient memory is unchanged under activation checkpointing. The gradient into the early blocks carries most of the learning. Branch loop/prefix.

ideas.title: Gold-aware stochastic keep
ideas.what: Per-document keep probability raised for gold documents but never 1 and never 0 for distractors, so the kept set does not reveal the answer; drop before block 0 as well as mid-stack.
ideas.result: Ten arms. Best: grJ, 0.133x dense per step, 0.172 held-out CE at step 108, 1.26x the recipe at matched loss. Others 0.75-0.89x; two 50-step Lambda arms 1.5-1.6x at a shallow level. Now being run deeper and on the mixed-length pools.

ideas.title: Loss and backward through the first few blocks only
ideas.what: An early-exit answer loss after block k gives true per-token gradients at full length for the cost of k blocks; use them to pick tokens and to train the early blocks.
ideas.result: Negative. Selecting tokens by the gradient of an early-exit answer loss is worse than the ridge router at the recipe's keep (0.213 vs 0.175 held-out CE at step 75) and at 10%/3% (0.237 vs 0.224); it only wins at a very aggressive cut after block 2 (0.584 vs 0.763 at step 40), far from any reference level. The auxiliary early loss slows training; training the early blocks by the early loss alone fails (0.503). The frozen head at block 7 gives an early-exit CE near uniform, so its gradient is weak. Branch loop/earlyloss.

ideas.title: Detached context / reused context states
ideas.what: Context tokens run forward-only (or reuse cached states), gradient only through query and answer tokens; then drop context tokens aggressively in that no-grad pass.
ideas.result: Negative for FLOPs. Context forward-only from block 0, no drops: 0.30x dense per step but 0.312 held-out CE at step 128 (0.15x of the recipe's efficiency); with the recipe's drops inside the no-grad pass 0.10x per step and 0.546 at step 168; every 4th step dense: 0.44x of the recipe. The context's own gradient carries most of the learning. Memory arms with activation checkpointing off still to read. Branch loop/detach.

ideas.title: FLOP-aware row sampling and row skipping
ideas.what: Sample rows by expected loss decrease per FLOP (short rows more often, a tail of 16k rows), skip rows a cheap early-exit loss marks as solved.
ideas.result: Recipe on rows <= 5k: 1.35x the recipe at matched loss at step 66; with 8 rows/step and LR 2e-5 0.98x; truncated rows 0.80x; dense LoRA on rows <= 5k 0.78x. Next: deeper runs, token-budget batches, length curriculum.

ideas.title: Label-consistent sub-problems
ideas.what: Train on a random subset of a row's documents with the answer rewritten for the subset (reorder, qdmatch), mixed with a few full rows.
ideas.result: Recipe on the 50/50 short/long pool: 0.159 held-out CE for 78 PF, 1.25x the recipe at matched loss; 80/20 pool 1.24x; short rows only 0.74x. Dense LoRA on the same pools is behind the recipe (0.66-0.90x). Deeper two-seed runs in progress.

ideas.title: Skip the FFN for context tokens
ideas.what: Context tokens stay in attention / GDN mixing but skip most FFNs, instead of leaving the sequence.
ideas.result: Negative. Body tokens skipping the FFN in blocks 0-6 with probability 0.5: 0.193x dense per step (the recipe is 0.220x) but 0.274 held-out CE at step 50 vs the recipe's 0.201. Skipping every body-token FFN in blocks 0-3 stops learning (0.779 at step 50): training adapts to FFN-free tokens and the dense eval forward runs every FFN. Ceiling of the idea: the FFN is 41-62% of a block's per-token FLOPs. Branch loop/ffnskip.

ideas.title: Start from a base with token-drop continued pre-training
ideas.what: Look for existing drop-CPT checkpoints and test whether aggressive dropping loses less from such a base. No CPT runs inside the loop.
ideas.result: Found: dropstruct token-exit CPT base (Qwen3.5-4B, tokens leave from block 8, 64M tokens of CPT) and its dense-CPT control, staged on mooney. Proxy runs from both bases queued for the new pool.

ideas.title: LR, batch size and schedule per FLOP
ideas.what: Cheap arms can afford more, smaller steps: rows per step, LR and warmup tuned per FLOP rather than per step.
ideas.result: Recipe at LR 2e-5: 0.85x; LR 4e-5: 0.61x; 8 rows/step: 0.74x; 8 rows/step at LR 2e-5: 0.62x of the recipe's efficiency at matched loss. Dense LoRA: LR 2e-5 slightly better than 1e-5 (0.126 vs 0.131 at step 100), LR 4e-5 worse (0.170).

ideas.title: Drop-CPT bases fine-tuned in their own token-exit format
ideas.what: Token exit at block 8 and at the input (first+last rule), from the matching CPT base and from the standard base, at fixed compression 0.2 / 0.1 / 0.05.
ideas.result: Input-level token exit (ratio 0.05-0.10) does not train from the standard base or the drop-CPT base (held-out CE 0.78-0.87 after 130 steps, at or above the starting loss). Block-8 arms still running.

best_by_hour.note: First 16k results; recomputed against the tuned reference (dense LoRA at LR 2e-5 is slightly better than at 1e-5). Worst-task speedup is at the 80-step level. One seed, eval_size 184.

best_by_hour.level: own final loss 0.159 (between the 50- and 60-step levels)
best_by_hour.note: Matched-loss ratio vs dense LoRA; 1.25x the recipe at that loss. Stopped by the 12-minute cap at step 143; a deeper two-seed confirmation is running. One seed, eval_size 184.

validation.arm: dense LoRA at f1 / f2 / f4, recipe at f1 (2 seeds) and f2, dense full FT at f1
validation.rows: 1,952 per task; evals 4 tasks x 4k / 8k / 16k, eval_size 500 per cell
validation.predicted: proxy: recipe 1.9x fewer FLOPs than dense LoRA to the 100-step loss level
validation.note: Establishes the real FLOPs-to-match on the new task set and checks the proxy's ratio. Agent started 01:30.

validation.run: full-epoch loss curves (488 steps, dense-forward held-out CE every 50 steps)
validation.note: Shows whether the recipe's FLOP advantage grows later in training, which a 100-step run cannot see.
